newsitem.title: UK: Drug-resistant bacteria spreads from chicken feed.
newsitem.headline: Drug-resistant bacteria spreads from chicken feed.

text.p: British scientists said on Friday drug-resistant bacteria could spread to people from animal feeds and praised bans on the use of certain antibiotics in them.
Ira Das and colleagues, microbiologists at City Hospital in Birmingham, described the case of a worker who got an infection after breaking his leg at a factory processing chicken carcasses.
They found the infection was full of Enterococcus faecelis bacteria that were resistant to the antibiotic vancomycin.
They tested chickens at the factory and found many were contaminated with vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE), which are found in excrement and gut contents.
The chickens had been given feed containing avoparcin, an antibiotic given to factory-bred birds to combat infection.
Antibiotics increase the growth rate of animals, but there are fears that routinely dosing animals with such drugs could give rise to antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

Das's group said this was the first evidence of this happening and spreading to people. "This is, to our knowledge, the first reported case of VRE infection where the probable source is animals colonised with VRE," they wrote.
"We welcome the decision of the European Union's Standing Committee on Animal Foodstuffs to ban the use of avoparcin in animal feeds."
The European Commission adopted the ban in January.
